newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian unions concerned over Colt buying Herstal.
newsitem.headline: Belgian unions concerned over Colt buying Herstal.

text.p: Unions at Herstal SA fear its suitor, Colt's Manufacturing Co of the United States, will turn the Belgian arms maker into a small supplier and export technological know-how to the U.S.

Colt is offering three billion francs ($82.4 million) for Herstal. It expects the Walloon region to put in one billion francs as well as give up its eight percent stake in Herstal and its veto right, the Belgian unions said on Thursday.
France's state-owned armaments group GIAT Industries was expected to contribute 9.1 billion francs, the unions said.
GIAT said earlier on Thursday it signed a letter of intent about the sale of its 92 percent stake in Herstal to Colt's.
GIAT said the deal was conditional on talks with Wallonia on an industrial plan, expected to be finalised in September.
Privately-owned Colt's said the acquisition would allow it to make the world's largest group of small calibre arms, uniting four top brands -- Colt, FN Herstal, Winchester and Browning.

Belgian union representatives presented Walloon prime minister Robert Collignon with an alternative for Herstal on Thursday. The plan should turn around Herstal with the help of the government and private investors before a search for reliable partners was started.
The unions called on GIAT to waive debts and cover operational losses at a total cost of nine billion francs.
Staffing would be cut by sending 420 people on early retirement at the age of 50.

The listing of half of FN Herstal's Browning division on the New York stock exchange -- a move also under consideration from Colt's -- would result in a capital gain of 1.5 to 2.0 billion francs for the restructuring, the unions said.

Collignon said in a statement Colt's would present a business plan in September. Wallonia would accept the takeover provided Herstal's activities would be kept in Liege, where the company was founded in 1889.
Herstal has a strong position on the military market with FN Herstal and on the hunting and amateur shooting market with Browning and Winchester.
Colt's, founded in 1836 in Hartford, Connecticut, by Samuel Colt, is currently controlled by investment group Zilkha.
